text: It worked for 3 weeks. I bought this washer from Menards on March 9, 2013. On March 26, it failed to drain any water from the drum. I tried the "drain and spin" cycle multiple times. Unplugged the power cord and plugged it back in. Nothing. It would try to spin, but wouldn't even try to drain. Tried to return it to Menards, but they wouldn't touch it, since it was past the 7-day return policy for major appliances. Called Whirlpool, and requested a refund, but of course, they would only schedule a repairman to come out in a few days. Both Menards and Whirlpool were in no mood to make the situation right, and simply stood by their policies, so I am following through with a negative review. If you want a washer than may break down in a few weeks, go ahead and buy it. I bought an old used Maytag so I could do laundry (likely at least 10 years old) and we like it more than the Whirlpool even when it was working. Bottom line: All the newer washing machines are going with electronic controls and high efficiency washing mechanisms. Not sure if any of them are any good, but I know this one isn't.[[ASIN:B00817F5FE Whirlpool 3.4 Cu. Ft. White Top Load Washer - WTW4930XW]]

Disappointed. This washer disappoints. I have done laundry for 20 years in numerous homes - I've probably used ten different washing machines and I thought they were all the same. I HATE this one. I was excited to save time, energy, and water. First, I didn't realize that this washer does not allow you to SOAK. There is no way to override the cycles and fill your tub with water to soak stains. I'm finding it nearly impossible to get stains out now. It spins the quality right out of your clothes, leaving everything extremely wrinkled and stretched. When I called customer service about this, they told me I was supposed to be seperating everything into very specific load types...which kind of defeats the purpose of having a big tub. I am doing MORE loads than with my previous washer! (and if you get the matching dryer, it does NOT take the same amount of time as promised. In fact, I'm often having to run the dry cycle twice - and yes, it's installed properly.) If you are short, DO NOT purchase this machine as you will not be able to reach the bottom of the tub. I'm finding I have to set the extra rinse and/or wash things more than once, because clothes come out smelling dirty or not having the HE soap rinsed out completely. I am only using the LOW spin cycle otherwise the clothes are beat up - again defeating the purpose of a green machine, since it takes more to dry in the dryer. It's impossible to hang dry clothes out of this machine, unless you want to iron every item. When I talked to customer service, they basically said tough luck and that as the consumer "I should have done more research." Um, maybe you just shouldn't have built the piece of junk. NOT GREEN. Not worth the $$$.

Love it!. Replaced my first generation Maytag Neptune with this washer. Three loads done and I love it! A bit of a learning curve when loading (don't just dump the clothes in, arrange around the center). Can't forget to mention the happy little tune when laundry is done! Looking forwards to many clean loads of laundry.

No matter what people tell you, DON'T BUY WHIRLPOOL.. I bought a Whirlpool Cabrio 580 and its partner (dryer) about 2 years ago. Just after the year warrenty expired (isn't that always true), the lid of the washer started to fall down instead of stay up when I was putting clothes in it. Then it would lift out of joint. It was still working, so I used it a while longer. Finally, it popped right out and I called Lowes where I got the machine. They sent someone out (who charged for a service call) who ordered a new lid (at somewhere around $150 or so) and came back to replace it. All in all, the replacement cost over $350. (over half the price of the original machine) But that wasn't all!!!!! A little after a year later, it popped again. Right now, I'm holding the lid down while it locks in place, and then it will work until the ending of the last cycle when it stops at one minute before finishing. Then I have to do a few more maneuvers to get it to finish properly. I don't know how long it will hold on like this, but it's very aggravating. I haven't put heavy things on the lid. Nor have I abused it in any way. I tried to call the company, and they have only four voice responses, none of which was anything to help my situation. Then the machine hangs up on you. I would never NEVER buy a machine from this company again, and would suggest that no one else do so either.

Stay away from LG. This review is for the LG dryer model DLEX8000W. I've owned LG Tromm washer and dryer pair at my prior residence and decided to purchase another set of LG washer/dryer for my new home. My past set of washer/dryer ran without problem for over 5 years, but this time I wasn't so lucky and currently experiencing the displeasures of dealing with LG customer service for the first time. When you buy an LG, make sure that the vendor you're purchasing the unit from will own up and exchange for a manufacturer's defect. My dryer unit ARRIVED defective, and made a very loud hammering noise and vibrations upon cold start from the moment it was turned on for the first time. The vendor I purchased the unit had me contact LG warranty service, or I had to pay for the return shipping in upwards of $300-500 - please note that it seems most online vendors have a similar policy when dealing with an LG defect. The only feasible replacement option was to go through LG warranty service, and LG sent out local warranty technicians three times (one appointment a no show) who could not determine the cause of the problem after taking the unit apart completely several times. The last tech sent out called LG tech support, and they assumed that the problem was with a worn turbine, rubber bushing and a washer that'll need to be replaced. If that doesn't work, they may replace the entire dryer drum that could be dented although it doesn't look dented at all??? wow - how is that a brand new dryer unit was shipped with WORN parts? Doesn't LG QA their appliances before shipping new products? The bottom line is that LG customer support is horrible and full of attitude, and they're completely adamant about their policy that unless a unit is deemed "unrepairable" by their own tech line, you'll get many warranty service visits and parts replacements even with a brand new unit. At one point, they even noted that my dryer noise is normal until I sent them another set of videos to prove otherwise. I've had my dryer for less than 30 days, but it is full of scratches (from the clumsy techs) and I completely regret purchasing it online. Even if the unit noise gets fixed with further parts replacements, the appliance has already suffered quite of bit of strain on its body/motor that probably reduced its lifespan. Do yourself a favor and get it from your local appliance store, and know that LG customer service is rated 547 to 25, a whopping 96% negatively reviewed under Customer Service Scoreboard. I am completely disappointed with LG, and I'll stay away from the brand.

The machine is on visit 3 from Fred's. I had a Kenmore 417.43142200 prior, its paired to a 628.9468213 dryer - still works fine. We talked about the old Maytag that went 20 years, the Whirlpools that went 10, but were easy to fix. He warned the Maytags are made by Whirlpool now (still a pretty good brand I thought, he didn't confirm.) I asked what he'd buy, he said "LG makes a good machine, Samsung..." I said, you'd think American industry would learn their lesson (cars), you mean were doing this again with appliances? I went to Sears first, with my paper work, before I got this Whirlpool, they might make a deal...? Well, no, but, I found they now private label Samsung and LG as Kenmore. So they moved on, as I should have. The Extended will probably get me through to a reasonable service life for the dryer. If I'm not unemployed, I'll pick up a new set of LG's in 2-3 years. If I am unemployed then, I won't be for long, I can fix these lousy machines 50hrs a week, and buy a dented pair of LG's. Don't Buy - The absolute worst. This washer came brand new in the place I'm staying at and it is the absolute worst. I don't understand the good reviews here. The machine starts agitating with no clothes in it. Then unbalances itself, then adds water to try to fix the imbalance and goes through this endless loop of adding more water, getting unbalanced. It doesn't have this problem on all loads, it is just inconsistent enough to be a headache. It twists the clothes into knots. It doesn't add enough water for clothes to be clean since it is "efficient" and it has gotten worse over time. The cycles take forever (>1 hour). You have to turn it off completely to adjust any settings. It has been approx 9 months since it was first used. It appears to be a design flaw with the way the machine works not that it is malfunctioning. We've had to wring out clothes by hand because waiting for it to be balanced enough to complete the cycle takes forever. It is the worst. I've never had these sort of problems with a washing machine. This LG washer is absolutely the worst washer I have ever had. I am 63 years old and have had numerous washers through the years. This LG washer is absolutely the worst washer I have ever had. I HATE this washing machine. We constantly get UE errors (uneven loads) no matter how carefully you mix and spread the loads. A load that should take 45 minutes to complete takes HOURS. It does so because the washer attempts to correct itself before shutting down by constantly draining, refilling, and re-agitating in an attempt to spread the load to its liking; then another UE is experienced and it drains again, refills, agitates. It continues to repeat this cycling until it finally shuts down. You start it back and it begins this process all over again. This is the worst designed washing machine surely any company has ever released to the public. Buy it only if you enjoy extreme frustration and high water and electric bills. This is the last washer I will ever purchase from LG.

If I could give it ZERO stars, I would!. Let me start by saying that because of my experience, I will never again buy ANYTHING with the Frigidaire or Electrolux name attached to it. NEVER. I bought my dryer a couple of years ago, and thought that only a one year warranty was a little shoddy, but never did I expect that the control panels in these dryers are like self-destructing "screw the customer" systems! The dryer started beeping one day while not even turned on, and displaying error code E68, the code for a stuck button. There are no buttons stuck, and upon researching it a bit, I found hundreds of other people online with the same exact problem. The control panel shorts out after 2-3 years and will cause the dryer to think a button is being held down and won't run. Nothing is wrong with the mechanics, it's all just this stupid electronic panel. As I, and the hundreds of other people with these dryers, have found out, Frigidaire absolutely refuses to replace the faulty control panel unless you pay ~$200.00 plus the cost of a service person to come put it in if you don't know how to do it yourself! They KNOW that they are selling dryers with defective control panels, yet hide behind their wimpy one year warranty as a way to milk a ton of extra cash out of their customers. Where is the recall, Frigidaire??? Hopefully the Better Business Bureau will care to urge them toward resolving this. In the meantime, I recommend that you DO NOT BUY THIS DRYER, OR ANY OTHER FRIGIDAIRE PRODUCT! THEY ARE SCAM ARTISTS!!!

Timesaver, Quiet, lowcost to run. I have this combo about 6 months now. Even though we live in a new home which has a perfect vent out, the main reason for buying this machine is to gain time and space (literally). We read through many reviews of the previous model and there were issues with the drying (wrinkles). Due to the fact that this machine has a larger capacity, this wrinkling have been greatly reduced. I have actually just one pants that is made of rough thick cotton and it's the only one that is clearly more wrinkled compared to using a separate (air) dryer. However, we found already ways to minimize it and that is to use the post-wash tumbling option (you can choose to let the machine tumble intermittendly when it's all done, to prevent wrinkling). This is a smart move from LG. Apart from that, this machine is just the best, I wouldn't know why you want to buy a separate washer and dryer: During the day we throw in cloth and usually we set the delay time as "switch-on around 3am" and the next morning you take the cloth out, ready to use, no more pain in remembering to put the cloth from washer to dryer. The machine is also so quiet that you can indeed do the above, it's a simply a whisperer. We are quite "green" so this machine is for us, the energy usage is so low compare to standard washers and dryers, mainly due to the condense drying system. Standard dryers are like a combination of many hairdryers and you know ho wmuch wattage they have. Last but not least, you safe so much space by eliminating 1 machine (dryer). Great machine!

Don't worry about the negative reviews this thing awesome and drys great too!. I'm rating this 5 stars, although there are some areas for improvement I think the 4 star rating on amazon doesn't give this washer the credit it's due. I read through all of the reviews and was really on the fence about it. I read several people having issues with clothes drying properly. I also saw the guy that added parts because his had a lot of steam coming from the small rear vent that was dripping off the cold water line. I reluctantly went ahead and made the purchase because of the other positive reviews. It's a washing machine/dryer combo that just makes sense. Now the drawback to this setup is of course you can't wash a load and dry a load at the same time. The drying also does take longer. However the convenience more than makes up for this in the right household. We are a family of 4, with a toddler and a 7 year old. This machine works great for our family. After reading through the reviews the common consensus is it doesn't work properly if the drain is too high. I have a standard wall drain mounted 36 from the floor. I decided to spend the extra money on the pedestal to not only bring the machine up for proper function of the drain, but also the additional storage and luxury of not having to bend over so far. This was money well spent, and the drain works perfectly without having to lower it. The LG sidekick also apparently works with it, which might be something useful for the right people. It's basically another small washer that mounts below the standard washer in place of the pedestal. This might be nice for athletic wear or something that can't go through the dry cycle. We usually just wash anything that doesn't get dried as a separate load. Generally a load takes about 4 hrs to wash and dry. I set a Custom PGM with our most used settings. So all we do is hit Power, Custom PGM, and start and it does it's thing. We like to use normal wash/ hot/Extra spin/normal dry, Turbo wash and Fresh care. Fresh care will tumble your clothes periodically for up to 19 hrs. I believe without fresh care it will do 4 hours of tumbling. To activate fresh care you hold the steam button down for 3 secs before you start the cycle. It can't be activated mid cycle. But it does store in the Custom PGM if you set that. Turbo wash uses jets on the washing machine door to spay the clothes, and apparently more efficiently clean clothes. LG's website says it saves 20 mins on a wash cycle. it does look pretty cool when watching it use the turbo wash. You can turn the drum lights on by pressing and holding extra rinse button for 3 secs. They stay on for 4 mins. As others have mentioned it has some fun melodies it will play when turning on or after a cycle is complete. The volume can be adjusted between low, medium, high and off using the signal button before starting a cycle. I do highly recommend a liquid fabric softener. Which it does have its own dispenser for. Clothes come out much softer and without wrinkles. Without the softener they seemed wrinkled and stiff. Crinkled is a good word to describe it. With the softener they come out perfect. They also have dryer balls, i've seen some made from wool that might be a good option. I've been considering getting some to try. The clothes are quite hot when a cycle is complete. Very hot. You do need to let the heat dissipate a bit, they wont burn burn you but they are uncomfortably hot. What we usually do is run the machine at night with the Fresh Care and the next morning the clothes are much cooler and don't have that hot humidity with them. They just seem like a normal load from a typical dryer. I do really love this machine but it isn't without a couple flaws that I gladly overlook. For one there is no lint trap other than one part of the drain behind a door on the front. This means there is fair bit of lint that builds up on the door and around the door seal. One person mentioned getting some wipes for this, I didn't really know what they were referring to until I saw for myself. So far we have used our hands or wipes, but I think a brush might work best. Also, the first time we used the washer it ended up getting a water stain streak on the door, and haven't found a way to clean it. I'm not sure how or what caused it. Maybe our hard water. But its only one streak. Not a huge deal but is unfortunate. Lastly the plastic window makes a lot of squeaking if you press on it. Sounds kind of cheap because of this, but its plenty strong. That's all I can think of at the moment. I'll update this as we use it and think of other things. I was a little worried it wouldn't dry to our satisfaction based on some of the reviews but it really does great at drying. So if you're worried it wont dry properly for you, stop worrying, the only thing you might need to look at is the height of your drain.

Overal does wash & dry but involves a lot of maintenance and has a lot of issues for the price.. So I read a lot of reviews before purchasing this and will now contribute based on my experience so far. I did not purchase this new from Amazon but used off of Craigslist (about 1/2 the price) - supposedly it was bought in June of this year so it is only about 6 months old and still under warranty. The owner was selling it because he is a landlord who bought it for his tenant and the tenant did not like how long the cycles took. I bought it because we have an old house and very little room - it was kind of a compromise between myself and my partner as a better option might have been for us to purchase separate compact washer & dryer but he wanted a larger capacity. This machine is large - going from a compact portable washer to this was a big difference - make sure you have measured your space before purchasing. The combo will help us preserve vertical space but it did not help at all in floor/hall space. So here is what I have found so far... PROS: * does essentially what it is supposed to do - washes with very little water and definitely dries (I have not tried to overload this and have probably only filled it between 1/3 to 2/3's so far but clothes have come out more than enough dry (on "normal" setting). * feels fancy and fun with the lights & noise * takes up half the space of two full-size machines * a good amount of options for different kinds of clothes - although initially seems kind of complicated it's pretty straightforward to set up - and because it's front load will be pretty gentle on your clothes * clothes come out dry when they're done ( no need to be there to change them from washer to dryer ) * being able to set it on timer is nice - I am not comfortable letting this be on while not at home yet but it's nice to set it to go off an hour or two before I wake up CONS * this is a very expensive machine and for the cost I would expect it to work MUCH better out of the box than it does - it will require regular cleaning & maintenance to keep it in top working order - much more than a regular dryer would (I will go into details below) * it is difficult to level; or I should say - I have leveled it pretty well based on my level but it still started shimmying away when I had a larger load in - we do have the challenge of very out of whack old house floors but this machine seems to have issues when it comes to getting it leveled correctly. I found a good post here on how to deal with this (and it's on my to-do list): [...] * I was pleasantly surprised that the first load I put in estimated less than 2 hours time (it was not a large load but based on what I'd read I was expecting worse) - however (and I have read this an issue for others) - when it got down to 6 min left on the display it stopped at 6 min for about 15-20 min before finishing and moving on; I looked this up and found others having this issue - I am not sure if it's a maintenance issue of the dryer not working well enough or a sensor issue - some LG dryer reviews said you need to wipe the sensors off but on this machine I am not sure where this is; so far what I have done to try and alleviate this issue is 1) make sure to wipe the lint out of the door seal real well (not easy - more below on this); 2) do the drain pump maintenance (pretty easy); and just to make sure I have all my bases covered I am going to go ahead and take the machine apart to clean out where the lint supposedly gets stuck - since I haven't been the original owner - I'd like to see where it's at now before I have to do it again * lint lint and more lint: you have probably already read this is an issue. it very much is an issue. you will need to wipe the rubber door seal after each use and it is not an easy simple & quick thing to do as the seal has a deep fold in it that is not easy to get your fingers into and also lint will get stuck under the edge of the seal so you kind of have to go around and pull this up. plan on this taking a good 5 min and not being a fun task - this is an issue that really makes me have to give the machine a lower review - LG REALLY SHOULD DO SOMETHING TO TAKE CARE OF THE LINT collection because there is essentially none and, as you have probably read, it leads to a larger issue of the dryer eventually not working and requiring you to take apart the machine in order to clean it out (unless you want to hire someone) but a great instructions on how to do this are here: [...] * the door rattle on high spin cycle - this is another big deal breaker for me in regards to giving this a good review. I have read it as being an issue with other people too - as far as i'm concerned there's no excuse for this - it is loud and annoying. I may be able to get it to be less of an issue if I can get the machine better leveled - and I have also heard of people making their own dampener by stuffing some cardboard in between the door and machine - either way - not cool LG. basically there is not proper padding between the door and it has wiggle room (when shut you can kind of push on it yourself and hear how it will sound if it happened multiple times). * another note on noise: as others have wrote - the pump is noisy. nothing to say except that yes, it is, and it will go on and off throughout the whole cycle; think of it as a loud humidifier or old loud fridge motor noise; when the pump is not going off it's very quiet; our bedroom is upstairs and the noise will not be loud enough to wake us up - and if you have well insulated walls it may not be an issue for you either - but don't go into it thinking that this thing is going to be quiet if you have thin walls or floors * smell: it smells a bit moldy/musty; I am just running Tub Clean for the first time today - will update later to let you know if the smell is alleviated - I am going to assume that the previous owner may not have done this at all. * other random issues which I can live with: the instructions say to hold the spinsense button down for 3 seconds to activate - this is not working for me ( I read somewhere that it won't work if you have the dryer set to cycle on - I will try again and see if that solves it ); when I went to use the Spin/Dry cycle the timer showed it as going to take 5+ hours even though I put in a very small load and there was no way it should have taken that long - for some reason the machine didn't run it's own sensor but just automatically goes to 5 hours - you can solve this by choosing the timed dry instead "normal" or "more" Overall I would NOT recommend purchasing this machine at full price. There are too many maintenance and glitchy issues to spend this kind of money. But, if you can find it on sale or used - it might be what you need to deal with space issues. Just make sure you understand that you will have to spend time to maintain it correctly and yes, the overall cycle times on a full load are going to be much longer than they would be on a normal washer/dryer. There is a big learning curve on the tiny things you run into that won't really be covered in the manual and for which you'll have to consult other reviews, internet search, etc to solve on your own. If you're the kind of person who doesn't mind doing this - then this machine may work out for you. But if you're looking for a low-maintenance machine that you won't need to worry about - this isn't it.

If you want clean clothes. We bought two of these washer/dryer combos, one from Amazon and one from Home Depot. The delivery from Home Depot was late, Amazon was right on time. We use one at our home and the other is at our vacation home. A normal size load takes about 3 hours and usually comes out a little damp, but dries after sitting in a clothes basket for about 10 minutes. Small loads come out much dryer and usually take a little over 2 hours. The reason we wanted a ventless dryer was because clothes out of a normal dryer come out smelling dusty. You see, most dryers pull air off of the floor of your laundry room and blow that air through your clothes for about 45 minutes. Often laundry rooms are not the cleanest room in the house. Ventless dryers do not pull in dirty air, they heat up and dehumidify the air in a closed loop inside your dryer. Clothes come out smelling much cleaner, although a little damp sometimes. There are other advantages to this combo besides not needing a vent. It uses half the space since you only need one unit to wash and dry with, it plugs in to a normal 120 volt outlet, no need for dedicated 30 amp dryer outlet and of course there is no need to remember to come back later to switch the clothes from the washer to the dryer. This way if I put a load in right before I go to bed or leave the house they are done when I get up or return home, so in some ways it can actually save time. The reason for only 4 stars is that on both units we own, the drain pump broke after about 6 months, so I would recommend buying an extended warranty. In both cases LG was out within 2 days to fix it at no charge. A price I am willing to pay for cleaner, dust free clothes.

Great improvement by GE. After reading many reviews about washing machines before making a decision, I decided to purchase this GE washer. I've always liked GE products, but after owning one of their previous HE models for about four years and being terribly disappointed with it's performance I almost purchased a competitor's product. I'm happy that I didn't. Note that this is not a paid review. Now for the review: Cleaning - 4 stars. This top load HE washer gets clothes clean. I would rate my previous GE HE at two stars, so a great improvement. I considered going back to an agitator washer but worried about capacity and the detrimental effect that an agitator has on clothing. The only reason I didn't rate a 5 is that I haven't tried to clean grass stains yet. It's winter time here so I have no grass stains to work with. Capacity - 5 stars. The 4.6 Cu. Ft tub has plenty of room for larger articles, including a king size quilt that I recently washed. The last load washed consisted of 4 pairs of jeans, a pair of work pants, 6 shirts, including a 2X flannel shirt and a 2X sweatshirt, and a few pairs of socks. There are settings on the washer for washing jeans separately from other colored articles, but that isn't the way we wash laundry in our household. Features - 5 stars. As mentioned above, there are plenty of settings for your laundry, 13 total, including one to sanitize with Oxy. There six water temp settings, four levels of cleaning (light through extra heavy), and four levels of spin cycle from no spin through max. All are controlled with easy touch buttons. If that seems like a lot of choices, no worry. You can set the my cycle button to remember your settings. I especially like the slide out detergent and softener dispenser tray located at the top of the tub that mixes the detergent with the load as the washer fills. This also makes cleaning easy, although I've washed more than 30 loads and there is no residue showing yet. If you've experienced clothing stains in the past from fabric softener dispenser build-up, worry no more. For those who remember warm water rinse, that feature has also returned with this model. There is also a deep fill button, which I use frequently. Press that button and 5-6 more gallons of water are added. I like to see my clothes bathing in water. Also included is a deep rinse button, recommended for use with fabric softener. This uses a bit more water and increases cycle times over the 34 minutes they boast about, but I feel more at ease. The glass top makes it easy to see what is going on in there. Noise - 3 stars. This compares to 1 star on my previous washer. I don't worry a lot about noise as my washer isn't setting next to the television. It does make some odd noises during the wash, also not a bother to me. One drawback is the dreaded walk that washers sometimes do. The only time I've experienced this issue is when the load became unbalanced on the king size quilt. If this happens, press the pause button and wait about 30 seconds for the lid to unlock to situate the items in the tub. The washer walk and the fact that I haven't tried to clean grass stains yet is my reason for rating at 4 stars instead of 5. I could have spent up to $200 more for another competitor's top load or twice as much for a larger capacity front load but I'm happy that I didn't. We aren't a large family and the 4.6 capacity is plenty enough for us. If you fall into that category, do some shopping for the lowest price and I think you'll also be pleased.

Cleans well but "warm" water setting delivers cold water. I've only had my washer for two months, so I can't comment on the reliability of the product. But I'd like to caution anyone thinking about purchasing the Samsung WF210 that when you select the "warm" water cycle, it doesn't use warm water; it uses cold water. I checked my hose connections -- nothing wrong there; when I select "cold" I get a cold wash, and when I select "hot" I get a hot wash (well, kinda hot). Prior to turning on the washer, I also run the water in the sink next to the washer until it gets hot. I have the water in my water heater, which is also next to the washer, set at 145 degrees (ripping hot), so I know that's not the problem. But whenever I check the water temperature of a wash for which I've selected "warm," it's always cold. So now, if I want an actual warm water wash, I have to add hot water to the tub during the cycle. I've since read other sites where others have noticed this problem, and one said that Samsung intentionally set the hot water usage low in order receive an energy star rating. Whether there is any truth to this, I cannot say. To those who have given this product such high ratings, I'd be curious to know if you have checked to see whether it actually uses warm water when you select the warm water cycle. I have to take a star off, because I thought I was paying for a washer that gave me a "hot," "warm," and "cold" option. Another problem that I had was with the bleach dispenser. I put a diluted mixture of bleach into the dispenser and washed a load of colored towels. I know that you're not supposed to use chlorine bleach on towels, but I like the clean smell and don't mind them being slightly faded. What I DO mind is spots! With my previous top-loader, I'd add the bleach to the tub and let it start to agitate before adding the towels, but you can't do that with a front loader. I thought that it would dilute the bleach even further before adding it to the wash, but I was sadly wrong. So now, a brand new set of towels is spotted. My solution is to add the bleach to a gallon of water and add that to the wash during the cycle. Other than these two problems, I think that this is a good washer. My clothes come out pretty clean and they don't get beat up or tangled. But for the steps that I have to go through in order to get a warm wash or to use bleach, perhaps I should have stuck with my old-fashion top loader! I hope this helps you. UPDATE 8/30/2012 I contacted Samsung and explained the problem regarding the warm water setting. They were very helpful and actually arranged for a replacement washer. A technician came out and installed the new machine. Unfortunately, the new machine does the same thing; when I select "warm," the water still comes out cold.

Steam fresh a joke. Before purchasing this washer/dryer combo I owned a Whirlpool duet at my previous home. I thought I would try this LG since it got good reviews and when you view these machines in the store they are very sturdy and well-made. If you are buying this machine for the "steamfresh" feature because like me you don't want to iron shirts that laid in the dryer too long--don't! The cycle takes 20 mins to run, then it "fluffs" the clothes for 30 mins, then after removing them from the washer the manual says to allow the damp clothes to hang for 10 mins before wearing. ??? Now an hour has passed and you could've just ironed them or thrown them in the dryer would've done just as well! Not at all like the commercial! My shirt came out too wet to wear (as it mentioned) and looked as if water had been squirted radomly on it. After all that, I ended up putting it in the dryer. The manual suggested you don't put 100% cotton clothes for the steamfresh either--which is exactly what i bought it for! (My husband's golf shirts) As far as the steamwash feature--if you need your clothes shot full of hot steam because your clothes are unsanitary then you may need this. However, I used the steamwash today on hot water WITH bleach (I might add this cycle took 1 hr and 15 mins) and it still didn't get my socks clean! It works fine to use as a regular washer, but my opinion is it isn't worth the extra $300 I paid full these extra features. Also, the LG is very loud compared to the Whirlpool Duet. It has a loud whining sound when it gets ramped up. The first time I heard it I thought there was a motorcyle going by outside.
